s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of throat fullness, pain, and respiratory distress with localized inflammation and a mass-like structure at the base of the tongue
salient_findings: Rapidly progressive fullness in the throat
Local redness at the root of the tongue
Mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue compressing the epiglottis
key_facts: 3-day history of fever
Fever and rapidly progressive throat fullness
Pain on swallowing
Dysphagia
Dyspnea
Local redness at the root of the tongue
Leukocytosis with a left shift
Elevated C-reactive protein
Normal thyroid-stimulating hormone, triiodothyronine, and thyroxine levels
Mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue on flexible laryngoscopy
No thyroid gland identified in its normal pretracheal location on neck ultrasound
Non-homogeneous, contrast-enhancing area at the tongue base with peripheral calcifications on CT scan

differentials: Squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue
per_call: Squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue

shortlist.label: Lingual thyroid
shortlist.why_kept: Mass-like prominence at the base of the tongue and absence of thyroid gland in its normal location

shortlist.label: Ectopic thyroid tissue
shortlist.why_kept: Similarities with lingual thyroid, but considering the possibility of thyroid tissue in an abnormal location

shortlist.label: Thyroglossal duct cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a mass-like structure at the base of the tongue and potential connection to thyroid tissue anomalies

shortlist.label: Base of tongue abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of symptoms, localized inflammation, and presence of a mass-like structure

shortlist.label: Thyroid teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare possibility of a teratoma in the tongue base, which could explain the mass and thyroid function test results

raw.rationale: The presence of a non-homogeneous, contrast-enhancing area at the tongue base with peripheral calcifications and the absence of a thyroid gland in its normal pretracheal location are consistent with a lingual thyroid, which is ectopic thyroid tissue located at the base of the tongue.

rejected.label: Ectopic thyroid tissue
rejected.why: While ectopic thyroid tissue is a broader category that includes lingual thyroid, the specific location and presentation in this case make 'Lingual thyroid' a more precise diagnosis.

rejected.label: Thyroglossal duct cyst
rejected.why: Thyroglossal duct cysts are typically midline and do not usually present with the inflammatory symptoms seen in this case.

rejected.label: Base of tongue abscess
rejected.why: The presence of a non-homogeneous, contrast-enhancing area with peripheral calcifications and the absence of a normal thyroid gland suggest a thyroid origin rather than a simple abscess.

rejected.label: Thyroid teratoma
rejected.why: There is no indication of the complex, mixed tissue types that would be expected in a teratoma, making this diagnosis less likely.
